claims.text: Adding an ML-based correction to CALPHAD and first-principles DFT will enable accurate prediction of elastic constants in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The ML-enhanced CALPHAD and DFT approach will accurately predict lattice distortions in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Improved predictions of elastic constants and lattice distortions will significantly improve estimates of low phonon thermal conductivity relative to conventional models.
A robust training dataset and independent DFT validation will support the accuracy of the integrated model.
The ML-enhanced model can capture phase-stability parameters arising from multicomponent interactions.
The ML-enhanced model can capture complex lattice distortions arising from multicomponent interactions.
The ML-corrected model will detect subtle variations in elastic properties caused by lattice distortions.
The ML-corrected model will detect variations in phase boundaries caused by lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions in refractory high-entropy alloys enhance phonon scattering.
Traditional models miss important nonlinear multicomponent effects.
The integrated ML correction compensates for the nonlinear multicomponent effects missed by traditional models.
Accounting for the proposed effects will yield lower predicted phonon thermal conductivity.
The enhanced model will predict elastic constants with errors below 15% relative to experiment.
Improved elastic-constant predictions will correlate with experimentally observed low phonon thermal conductivity.
Conventional CALPHAD and DFT models typically have errors exceeding 15% for elastic-property predictions.
Conventional CALPHAD and DFT models typically have errors exceeding 15% for thermal-conductivity predictions.
The approach is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys that remain single-phase and thermally stable up to 1000 °C.
Predictive performance may decrease outside the calibrated composition range or in alloys with substantial phase segregation or secondary phases.
The approach's success depends on training-data availability and quality and on correctly representing multicomponent interactions.
Transferability to high-entropy alloys with compositional complexity beyond the training set is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says falsification requires both elastic constants and thermal conductivity to deviate by more than 15%, whereas the experimental rule says a deviation greater than 15% in either quantity is sufficient.
